title: Boombox
alt: And she's gonna feel like a jerk when she realizes it was actually Under Pressure.
transcript:
[Megan is looking out a second story window at Cueball holding a boombox over his head. Musical Notes are coming out of it.]
Cueball: Megan!
Megan: Oh my god, I can't believe this is happening.
Cueball: I love you!
Megan: Okay, that's great. Wait a second. Is... is that... Ice Ice Baby? What the hell?
Cueball: I'm not very good at this.
explanation:
This comic references a scene in the 1989 romantic comedy movie , where  plays 's  on a boombox outside the house of the girl he likes to declare his love. This emulates a trope that has often been used in fiction, most notably the "balcony scene" from 's play  (act 2, scene 2), and a similar situation in 's  (act 3, scenes 6-7). In the former, Romeo, attempting to woo Juliet, stands beneath her balcony to profess his love for her. In the latter, an inarticulate cadet, Christian, professes his love for Roxane by arranging to use the words of a fellow soldier, Cyrano, who secretly also loves Roxane.

Cueball tries to emulate this romantic moment for Megan, but screws it up by playing a decidedly non-romantic song instead. She first is startled and embarrassed by his declaration, but that gives way to confusion at his choice of the 1990 hit single  (video) by . There likely isn't any significance to the specific song being played here, because any other reasonably non-romantic song would have worked just as well. (For example, if Cueball had tried to romance Megan by playing Raining Blood, or the Price is Right theme song, she probably would have been equally unimpressed.)

The title text mentions that Cueball is actually playing  (video), the 1981 hit song by  and , but Megan has confused it with Ice Ice Baby, which samples the bassline and piano motif from Under Pressure. Young adults who grew up in the 1990s might hear the intro to Under Pressure (early 1980s), and mistake it for Ice Ice Baby (early 1990s). (It also may be that Cueball is having trouble holding the boombox, hence Cueball being 'under pressure.') His assessment that she's "going to feel a jerk" when she realises the mistake is probably misjudged, as she is likely to be more focused on his embarrassing behavior.

These two songs are referenced together again in 1561: Water Phase Diagram, and Ice Ice Baby is also lampooned in 210: 90's Flowchart. It is possible that this is the same couple as mentioned in 112: Baring My Heart, as the creator of that Venn diagram reveals to their romantic partner that their feelings towards their paramour are comparable to their feelings for Vanilla Ice. The same film scene is also referenced and parodied in the  episode 'Raisins', when Stan unsuccessfully tries to win back his ex-girlfriend Wendy in this fashion. Stan is advised to play Peter Gabriel out of a boombox, but plays the decidedly unromantic Peter Gabriel track . It is possible that Randall was also referencing that South Park scene in this comic.
